sensitivity.rule: the tlog_holdout verdict clips that share a group with a training row, read apart: each model's per-class error with them and without them (architect r3's sensitivity split); every other source stays whole

commit.rule: Step 6's carrier lines, never pooled across the correct and catch sides: the empty-slot rate where the mushaf prescribes a haraka (an omission) and where it prescribes a sukun (no written haraka, so an empty slot is the expected form); the commit rate and committed accuracy separately, because a unit may carry the haraka inside its consonant token; and teacher agreement for our students only, projected onto the teacher's vocabulary, a clone diagnostic that is never computed for zipformer

everyayah_heldout.note: no published name to look up; names prove nothing (qud_overlap.py)
everyayah_heldout.reciter: 3 EveryAyah reciters, unnamed in the benchmark

tlog_holdout.note: no published name to look up; names prove nothing (qud_overlap.py)

consumed.note: the rows the round-2 candidate read, not tlog.training's pool: a pool row the run never read is not exposure (architect r3, D3)

exposure.rule: each model's recordings-exposed share of the edit set's source and donor clips, over its full lineage (its round's uses plus the shared-baseline uses it inherited from h448), by the registry's source/alias rule; the reciter share is the weaker name screen, kept beside it. The teacher and zipformer trained outside Tadabur (unknown, not zero). A source or donor clip inside the candidate's lineage confounds the catch-side bar: a caught edit may be a memorised clip, not a caught mistake

card_gate_v3_decoder_check.stop: only 570 of 577 clips (0.9879) re-tokenise to their emitted units, below 0.9900, and 4 of 7 failures register a segmentation the model never emits: the longest-match stand-in is not the card's tokenizer, so no PER against it can be trusted

rule.cut_decisions: each check's units and every cut decision must agree; a decision sherpa's start frames alone leave open is resolved from the reference front end's own frame outputs (the trace phase), and stays a refusal, never a pass, while it is open
rule.every_planned_clip: the record covers the committed plan's clips, at the plan's own per-source counts; a partial run never passes
rule.frame_allowance: a start frame may shift only where no sampled cut changes (astra r1 §3)
rule.padded_final_chunk: no call may be padded: both runtimes stop before an incomplete chunk and their call counts must agree on every clip (rule 4, repaired in the diagnosis round)
rule.same_weights: ours and sherpa must decode the same ONNX: the identity's pinned sha256 is compared with sherpa's model record

match_rule.rule: single-stream checks matches checks-w1 when the paired 95% interval of the difference contains 0 on both metrics; then one stream suffices in the app

probe.rule: the checks-w1 store's audio-seconds per wall-second on 20 qdat items, projected over the batch's jobs at that point; the batch stops past 12 h (architect r2, AC 6). The Tarteel v1 confirm half was decoded afterwards as its own job, and its measured wall is in the compute table

report_only.rule: whole-item decodes only, no app check sequence and no ratchet: the reading of each model's ability without Muraja's engine in the loop, each on its metric arm (stream_b0 for ours, spans for zipformer)

qdat_bench.rule: the experts' phonetic_transcript, read on the Hub and never committed: each model's committed text on the clip's own audio, letter by letter over the transcript's slots, per class; and where the transcript leaves the mushaf (the departure words), which no model is scored on here

qud_other.arm_note: each arm's committed transcript from its recorded check sequence; zipformer's is the single stream's checks, ours the app's own per-check decodes
qud_other.rule: QUD's unread half, the frozen complement's segments of the pilot's two mushafs, scored against the corpus's truth sites (report only: zipformer probably trained on it). The round-2 candidate has no committed QUD decode, so its arm is named missing

sets.rule: the sets the cards say zipformer probably trained on are read beside the verdict, never inside it, and each arm's committed transcript is the arm the corpora's own readouts use. qdat_bench's expert transcript is read on the gated Hub and never committed; only its agreement summary is

tarteel_v1_confirm.arm_note: each arm's committed transcript from its recorded check sequence; zipformer's is the single stream's checks, ours the app's own per-check decodes
tarteel_v1_confirm.rule: Tarteel v1's confirm half (the look half is decoded for three of the four arms), scored against the corpus's truth sites (report only: zipformer probably trained on it)

ship_a.rule: sites are split by the human verdict only: correct recitation, a real mistake, or (unclear/pending) no side, which leaves both denominators and is reported apart

commit_rate.reason: sparse or degenerate, and not independent and equally weighted

truth_sites.rule: the canonical truth-site read on the same sites: each arm's committed transcript, no Muraja engine; correct and mistake sides never pooled

ship_a_mistakes_flagged.note: over the whole verified population (75 mistake sites)

verdict.rule: GO = the correct side closes half the gap on qdat and tlog_holdout and the catch side is within the candidate's minus 5 points (decoys >= 95%); PRIOR = correct passes, catch fails; STOP = correct fails
